Subject: SIG: Request for full third-party/subprocessor roster (cloud, telemetry, support)

Hi Priyom,

Following up on our vendor assessment intake — Acme Payments is finalizing its SIG review and we need a comprehensive subprocessor/third-party roster from Redwood covering: cloud providers (IaaS/PaaS used for prod and staging), telemetry/observability vendors, error/event collection and analytics, customer support/ticketing platforms, on-call/alerting providers, and any identity/KMS/HSM providers that have access to customer data or keys.

Can you provide:
- A single spreadsheet listing vendor name, purpose, data accessed (tokens, logs, backups), country of hosting, and whether you have a DPIA/flow-down clause in your contracts.
- Any SOC 2/ISO artifacts that reference subcontractor management (or pointer to where we can download them).

We need this for compliance signoff; target deadline: 2025-11-18 COB. If anything requires an NDA or additional access, flag it.

Thanks,
Elena Romero
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments

Looks good. Couple of asks from my side before we send externally:
- Confirm whether Intercom is configured to persist full transcript for enterprise accounts — for some customers we enable transcript suppression. If it does persist, we should mark the data access as "customer content" and note retention policy.
- For Datadog: confirm whether request-level traces contain prompt text for hosted customers. My note: token sampling is enabled, and full request traces are not stored in Datadog by default; we store metrics and aggregated traces.
- KMS/HSM: confirm who controls CMK rotation (we do, via AWS KMS; CloudHSM used for hardware-backed key storage for certain tenants).

If you want, legal can add a one-paragraph flow-down excerpt, but procurement needs to sign off on any vendor that will have access to customer secrets (that should be marked red).

Michael Grant
Head of Trust & Security Operations
security@redwoodinference.com

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is our completed subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessor_roster.xlsx) and a short summary PDF (sig_answers_summary.pdf) that calls out the key items you asked for:

Executive summary (excerpt):
- Cloud providers: AWS (prod, backups, KMS/CloudHSM), GCP (staging), Azure (CI runners); country/region columns populated in the sheet.
- Telemetry/observability: Datadog (metrics/aggregated traces, no full prompt storage), Sentry (errors, PII scrubbing enabled), Prometheus (internal metrics).
- Support/ticketing: Intercom (support chat; retention configurable per customer), Zendesk (ticketing for hosted support).
- Identity/KMS: AWS KMS (CMKs managed by Redwood), CloudHSM (hardware key protection for select customers), HashiCorp Vault (secrets management).
- Data access: row-level "data_access_notes" in the sheet indicate whether the vendor can access request content, metadata only, or admin logs.
- Contract flow-down: standard subprocessor clause is included in our Master Services Agreement; for customers requiring explicit flow-down language we can provide a one-paragraph excerpt (legal/procurement).

Links and artifacts:
- Download roster + details: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwood/Subprocessors-Inventory
- SOC 2 reference: Redwood SOC 2 report available on our security portal (link provided after an NDA) — contact security@redwoodinference.com to request access.

If you want, Michael can join a short call to walk through the items marked as "security critical" (HashiCorp Vault, CloudHSM). Let me know a window and we'll set it up.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
